text:
The entire lobby and breakfast area is being remodeled. Carpet has been pulled up, walls & furnishings updated, and the breakfast area is in a temporary room with food set up on folding tables. No hot food other than microwaved sausage, egg, & cheese biscuits. Staff was friendly. Avoid the end rooms, as ours was 435 and had a VERY small 'closet' and very small desk. Bath counter was small also. The beds were great, and the room was very clean, though. Our maid left cute and ingenious towel art on our bed each morning (see photo), which earned a tip.
If we could have had a normal room with a normal closet, and they were done with the remodeling, it would probably be a great place.

text: I have stayed at this hotel many times over twenty years of travel. And every time I have stayed here it has been due to a cancelled fllight or a missed connection. And this past week it was not different. A flight cancellation and missed connection equaled a night at the Hilton O'Hare. This time it included my husband and daughter and with a late arrival we were both tired and hungry. The check-in process was simple and the staff offered small bottles of water while waiting to check in. While the rooms are smaller than a usual Hilton, they are clean and perfectly fine for a one night stay. The restaurant was closed by the time we arrived, but the sports bar was still open. Burgers and chicken wings were perfectly fine. The wine prices were outrageous but the beer was in line. The continental breakfast in the morning was well above average. If you have an early morning flight, or if you are stranded for the night, this is an incredibly convenient hotel, (you never have to walk outside) with great service and good food.
label: positive

text: Spotless Garden Inn - meets all expectations. Fitness center is available 24 hours, but the pool is more limited This is new, like the IND airport terminal, and so neighborhood amenities have yet to develop. Therefore, if you don't have a car, you could be stuck. Finally, I did notice airplane traffic, but was not bothered by it. Appeared that flight path was in front of the hotel - rooms on the back side might be slightly better, but not sure. Other reviews seemed painted a pretty accurate picture of what to expect.

text:
Immaculate rooms, a lovely hot cooked breakfast buffet and a staff that made the hotel better than any four star one I've stayed at. We came for a funeral and all the extended family stayed here. When they learned we were all from out of town and had no home to get together at, the staff invited us to gather in the breakfast room. They made us so welcome. We sat by the fireplace and reminisced. It was quiet and comfortable. 
The location is ideal- we had people fly into SFO and San Jose, and had relatives from various California cities, and the hotel is conveniently situated near multiple freeways, close enough to make reaching it a perfect meeting point.
A hotel can be well located, completely well appointed like this one, but the heart and soul of hospitality is the staff. This one went above and beyond. All it took was letting us use a public area but they made us feel welcome and that made all the difference.
The only weakness I found about this hotel was an odd one... the signal strength for multiple cell phone carriers was awful, a surprising thing for Silicon Valley.
label: positive

text:
The location was very convenient and while the staff were friendly, they insisted that we use the electronic check in option instead of helping us themselves. Why pay staff if they are just going to direct you to the auto check in??? Which, funnily enough, wasn't working properly and they had to check us in themselves. 
We got home from dinner about 10:30 and proceeded to hear our neighbors have sex. To be fair to them, they weren't being that loud, its just that the walls were paper thin. Awkward. Despite being on the 9th floor and facing an alley, we could hear everything on the street below. I mean I could hear the conversations of the people as they left the bar at 2:30 a.m. and randomly at 5 a.m. there was a crazy person screaming at the top of their lungs for about 5 mins. Granted, its not the hotels fault that there are crazy people on the street or that drunk people tend to be obnoxiously loud. What the hotel could use is some double glazing as I don't think its too much to not hear the street noise from 10 stories up.
label: negative

text:
This is the most expensive hotel I have ever stayed in my entire life but it rates near the bottom in terms of quality. If I had paid the $450 per night the Grand Hyatt charged out of my own pocket I would have checked out after the first night. However, I was tagging along with my wife while she was on business in DC so I only have to wonder why a hotel could charge so much money for a basic room. No this was not a suite, it was a room withtwo double beds.
First the good. When you walk in, the lobby truly looks grand. But this is DC and this is the kind of hotel people stay in when somebody else pays the bill. The breakfast, while expensive ($21 for the buffet) was good. I especially liked the omelets. Service was friendly. We had drinks at The Cure a very relaxing bar. While expensive ($20 for a glass of merlot and a draft beer) the bartender was friendly and efficient. The check in was quick ut when we inquired about the price of wi-fi access the clerk did not know. I decided to live without e-mail for a few days since I was on vacation. What else is good? The location. My wife was able to walk to her meetings offsite and I was able to get to all the tourist hotspots in about 15 minutes.
Now the mediocre. While the lobby was great, we did not sleep there. We slept in what was essentialy a $100 a night room. The beds were comfortable enough and the TV was big, but everything else was rather underwhelming. The bathroom was dimly lit, there was no exhaust fan that we could find, and the toilet seat was broken. The towels looked like somebody bought the cheap ones at a Wal-Mart. The AC unit was on its last legs. We called maintenance to have them look at. They determined it was working OK, and despite it only being about 60 outside, we "just had to turn it all the way down and leave th blower on high". I pity the poor blokes who stay in 247 in July. Apparently the maid's vacuum didn't work either because the floor didn't appear to be vac'd during our stay.
So all in all, a rather unimpressive hotel. I was expecting much more.
label: negative

text:
Residence Inn is great hotel chain on the whole. My family always tries to find one when we visit a new US state. There's always comfort, complimentary food, good wifi, a kitchen complete with a tea/coffee service, stove, fridge/freezer, dishwasher & cupboard with dishes. Great if you want to buy groceries & cook your own meals to save money or have a late night snack. 
What made this DC location great was that it was a few blocks away from a lot of the main attractions & great restaurants. The hotel supplied me with a four-paged handout list of all nearby restaurants. An added plus is that this particular Residence Inn is right next to a pharmacy that also sells groceries, so everything you need for your room is a few feet away from your door.
Service was great, everyone who worked there was helpful & mannerly. The glass door of the closet was accidentally shattered when we tried to squeeze a huge suitcase into the closet. The front desk sent a repairman to our room to check it out, he left & returned with a new glass door to install and in 12 minutes it was as if nothing had happened. What was even nicer was the fact that the hotel didn't charge our room for the accident.
I definitely recommend this hotel, especially if you are traveling with family or friends. Just know that they charge (as of April 2012) $29 a night for parking AND that there's a height restriction because the parking lot is underground. Unfortunately, the huge jeep that we rented was too tall to fit into the RI lot, so we had to park up the road in another hotel's parking lot for $32/night. 
If you can help it, save the cash & don't rent a car at all - regardless of which you hotel you stay in, unless you plan on exploring in your car outside of DC into the wider DMV area. Between the rental fee & insurance and parking fees both at the hotel and around the main streets & major spots in downtown DC, it adds up. Walking is healthier anyway. lol
label: positive

text:
I stayed with the Erwin over the weekend and had a great stay! The hotel staff was very helpful and friendly and the room itself was fresh and comfortable. I work in the hotel industry and have stayed at a lot of hotels. I give the Erwin two thumbs up. 
The bed at the Erwin was comfortable, which ranks high on my requirements given my propensity for back problems. You can't beat the location and if you've got a little extra to spend then I highly recommend getting a room with a view and on the 6th floor. The 6th floor has balconies, so you can order room service and have breakfast outside looking at the beach. There is a rennovation taking place, but it didn't disrupt my stay. Asdies from some scaffolding outside, I didn't notice it. 
There aren't many restaurants off the boardwalk in Venice, so make sure you make a reservation at High (rooftop bar) or the . It has panorama views of the beach and good food/drink. It's got heat lamps too, so whether it's a sunny day or you want to kick back at night...High is the place to be. Also, Barlo, the restaurant off the lobby, has a great breakfast.
If you've never stayed at a Joie de Vivre hotel, it's worth checking one out. They all have charm, good quality of the rooms and great service.
label: positive

text:
I am so glad I gave this place a try. I usually stay at Hilton properties – in Chicago the Palmer House or the Wit (although I have tried the Hampton Inn around the corner when the town was booked up with conventions). I think I may have found my new home in Chicago. 
As A Hilton Honors Diamond, I was greeted and acknowledged (nice touch that happens too infrequently at other Hilton properties). I was upgraded to a very nice room (1211) which had a great view of the Hancock tower, the water tower and Michigan Ave. up to Oak Street Beach. Really great! The room was squeaky clean a very spacious. The bathroom was huge as was the entry way. I overheard a guy on the elevator say that 1209 (right next door) was his favorite room at the hotel – so I guess I did well. I liked the high tech entertainment system which had nice Bose speakers and all sorts of hook ups for iPod, other aux., laptop, etc. I was glad the remote came with instructions (wasn’t intuitive) and that the maid put the remote back with the instructions each visit.
I used the gym (well outfitted with what looks like brand new equipment). The only downside was that it was in a windowless room on the 11th floor. But it was great to get in, get it done and get out. I liked that they offered cold towels and headphones in addition to the normal water and dry towels.
I ate breakfast at the restaurant twice (very nice service and very accommodating). The HH breakfast voucher was good for two specified full breakfasts (one healthy and one hearty) or $19 credit. I am on a crazy diet and was able to find great stuff to eat , modified to my requests, very easily with very little in the way of “up charge.” I do think that those without the HH voucher will find the breakfast very expensive (oatmeal and fruit plate was $21). I also ate lunch one day on the terrace off the lobby. Over $40 (with tax and tip) for a very small piece of salmon and a side of steamed asparagus (no drink other than water) seems excessive for lunch in the only restaurant at the hotel. . . .) But I have to admit it was good and I was on an expense account.
The few requests that I made were met with enthusiasm and competence – I appreciate that. Checkout was a friendly breeze and I was on my way. The only wrinkle was that I left my Bose noise-cancelling headphones in the room safe. I didn’t realize it until I was on the plane at ORD. A call to the hotel had them promising to call me back with the status. Not 10 minutes later, before they shut the cabin door, they called to say they had it and would send it to me (charged my credit card – not free or anything – which I sort of this a hotel of this stature should do for a top-tier frequent guest . . . . but I digress). 
Overall, I am a very satisfied guest who will be returning.
label: positive

text: We celebrated our 25th wedding anniversary with a two day stay at the Hotel Monaco in Baltimore, Maryland. Built in 1906 as the headquarters for B&O Railroad, most of the architecture and detail was carefully restored in the Beaux Arts style. The hotel’s lobby area features a spacious lounge with a complimentary afternoon wine hour. Beautifully appointed rooms. Ours was handicapped accessible. Management and staff were very attentive and accommodating. The B&O American Brasserie is available for meals (on the street level).

text: I must say that I traveled to New York last week for the first time. I enjoyed every bit of it that I want to go back again! I was able to check in early and they were nice enough to hold my suitcase for me while I toured the town until my official check in time. I find this hotel convenient to the subway. There is Starbucks right across the street which was really nice since I'm a coffee drinker! I traveled by myself and was able to get a double bed! It was nice because I was on the 20th floor and the view was ok....seeing rooftops and other buildings. I didn't feel like I was in a hotel though. I felt like I was in a penthouse. The bed was very comfortable. I have no complaints. The only thing is that the shower stall curtain is short. So that means when you take a shower, water still ends up on the floor. I didn't mind because the housekeeper gave me plenty of bath towels and I used that to clean up the water. I will definitely return again!

text: Booked room on hotwire, so the location was great for the price. The check-in staff allowed us in shortly after 1pm, which was very appreciated. Overall the hotel is fine, rooms average. We were provided a room with two double beds. We tried to share the bed initially, but learned that it was just not enough for my husband and I to share. The pillows were very uncomfortable too, but luckily our stay was only for one night. My biggest issue would be the staff in the lobby bar. We did not have a pleasant experience there- the staff seemed irritated that we were asking for drinks. I would just recommend avoiding that part of the hotel, and you should be fine. We got a deal on the hotel through Hotwire, so I was fine with what we got. I would not have been happy had we paid full price for the room.
